description: Hi, I'm Harshini. I enjoy learning new concepts, exploring creative ideas, researching real-world problems, and developing technical solutions. I am excited to explore the untold stories of NASA's past missions through this challenge. I am interested in collaborating with people who have skills in programming, web development, UI/UX design, 3D modelling, animation, storytelling, and data visualization. I believe in learning together, sharing ideas, and creating something meaningful.
summary:
NASA Mars Explorer is an interactive web adventure which allows children to explore the fascinating stories behind NASA’s silent Mars missions. Many spacecrafts have completed their missions or become silent and are left floating in space or on Mars. Most of us have never thought of them.

Children play as young explorers. They log in to their account, launch a rocket to Mars, and meet a friendly talking guide to Mars. They will then be able to explore six different missions. Each mission involves solving a jigsaw puzzle using real data from the spacecraft, listening to the story behind the mission, completing a quiz and earning points and a badge. There is a timeline of each mission showing when they were launched. Children can use their points to upgrade their own rocket in the workshop. They will also receive an explorer certificate once they complete a mission.

We aimed to make learning about space history easy, fun and emotional. Children will develop their curiosity around space science by learning through play. They will learn that although these spacecrafts are abandoned they are not forgotten. The app was created using real data and images from the NASA missions.
details:
Project Description –NASA Mars Explorer

Project Title: NASA MARS EXPLORER

Project Theme: Tell a story about retired NASA equipment.

The NASA MARS Explorer

Project is an interactive educational website aimed at children between the age of 8 and 12. This helps children learn about the stories, achievements and scientific contributions of NASA’s historic equipment.

The children begin by taking a fun animated journey to Mars. They will meet a friendly character who will tell them about Mars. They can then interact with the six levels of equipment. Each level contains information about a mission including Sojourner, Mars Pathfinder, Ingenuity, Viking, Kepler, NEAR Shoemaker and Spirit and Opportunity.

Each level has:

A puzzle game to piece together a 3×3 picture using NASA equipment images.

A story told by the equipment. This tells the children how the equipment went on its mission, what it discovered and its achievements. The information is delivered simply using first person dialogue.

Information about the scientific side of the mission. Children can look at the timeline, instruments, measurements and history of the mission.

A quiz section to test what they have learnt. They will be rewarded for getting the right answers.

Points and badges. Children can earn points and badges for completing activities.

A rocket workshop. Children can use the points they have earned to upgrade their rocket in different ways.

Once the children have completed all 6 missions, they will have earned all the badges and upgraded their rocket they will have unlocked the Mars Explorer achievement. The website also has voiceover so children can listen to the stories.

This helps children learn about space science in an easy, fun and interesting way.

Benefits

Improves awareness of space science. Children learn about NASA’s historic missions and equipment.

Interactive. Children use puzzles and quizzes to engage with the information.

Improves problem-solving skills. Children use the image puzzles to think logically and observe.

Improves scientific knowledge. Children learn what each instrument, equipment and mission was for in simple terms.

Encourages curiosity. Children become curious about how the missions work and what the scientists have discovered.

Self-paced. Children can take their time to learn about the missions.

Rewards. Children are motivated to learn by earning points, badges, certificates and upgrading their rocket.

The main aim of our project is to raise awareness of NASA’s historic equipment and missions.

Many children know about famous missions and current rovers but may not know about the older equipment.

We have brought these missions to life by using interactive stories. We aim to:

Educate children about the history of space exploration.

Help children understand the scientific contributions from past missions.

Increase interest in astronomy, space technology and engineering.

Encourage future generations to pursue a career in science and technology.

Show that even though a mission has finished, the scientific contributions and discoveries are still very valuable.

We aim to turn forgotten equipment into memorable learning experiences.

We created a full stack website.

Frontend: React.js, HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Backend: Node.js, Express.js

Database: MongoDB, Mongoose

Authentication: JSON Web Token (JWT), bcryptjs

NASA information: NASA APIs, NASA mission information.

Voiceover: Web Speech API

Animations: Canvas Confetti, CSS animations.

Tools: Visual Studio Code, Node.js, npm.

Deployment: Vercel.

No special equipment is needed. The website can be accessed on any device with a web browser and internet connection.

Creativity

We have combined information about NASA missions with stories and gamification.

Rather than just putting information about the equipment in articles we have let the equipment tell its own story.

Some creative aspects of this project include:

Storytelling using the equipment. Historic equipment becomes a character and interacts with the children.

Interactive. Children piece together images of NASA equipment.

Voiceover. Children can listen to the stories.

Gamification. Children are rewarded with points, badges, quizzes and achievements.

Rocket workshop. Children can personalise their exploration rocket using rewards from learning activities.

Journey. The children go on a journey from Earth to Mars, explore the missions and return back to Earth.

The unique idea was to combine the history of space exploration with an exciting journey for children. This makes the scientific information easy to understand and remember.

As a team we had a shared goal to make space science fun and easy to understand for children.

We had a range of roles to complete:

Research. Researching information about NASA missions, equipment, instruments and discoveries.

Content. Turning technical information into simple stories for children and creating quiz questions.

Frontend. Creating the user interface, animations, puzzles, stories and interactive activities.

Backend. Adding authentication for users, keeping track of progress, points and managing data.

Integration. Integrating the different modules and ensuring they work. This improved the user experience.

Working as a team allowed us to combine our scientific research, creativity and coding into an educational platform.
